Recipe:
Dutch Oven Fried Rice 8-10 Servings (or 15-20 if just used as a side dish)
Based on a Recipe from Joy of Cooking
12&inch; Dutch Oven
§ion;
Ransom used the recipe book Joy of Cooking while on his mission. (It is still his favorite hard-copy recipe book.) When he got home from his mission, he adapted the recipe to be an entree cooked in a Dutch Oven.
Vegetable Oil½-1 Cup Uncooked Rice4 Cups Water6 Cups Salt1 teaspoon Eggs4-6
Hamcut into ¼&inch; chunks 1-2 Cups
Chinese CabbageShredded 1-2 Cups
CarrotsSliced Thinly ½ Cup
OnionsCut into ½&inch; &by; 1&inch; ½-1 Cup
Soy Sauce2-4 Tablespoons
Place Dutch Oven on medium amount of charcoals. Add Oil and Uncooked Rice and saut&eAcute;, stirring/scraping frequently until Rice begins to brown. Add Water and Salt and stir well. Cook with the lid on, stirring occasionally until Rice is cooked. (≈20-45 minutes)
Dig as large of a hole as possible in the center, all the way to the bottom. Then add Eggs and stir them (not Rice) until they are small fully-cooked pieces.
Add Ham, Chineese Cabbage, Carrots, and Onion then stir and let steam for 5-10 minutes. Add Soy Sauce and stir very well.
Instead of Chinese Cabbage, use Celery Greens Replace some or all of the Onions with Scallions cut into ½&inch; lengths. If it just going to be a side dish, the amount of Ham can be reduced or left out completely. Instead of Ham, use pre-cooked Chicken or Beef pieces.
